lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with a few basics:

1. **How many children do you have or are responsible for?** Please provide their names and ages.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking into whether I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask you a few questions about Alex to determine your eligibility.

Since Alex is 19 years old, the key question is: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they remain in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still studying - he's doing his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. A-levels at sixth form college would typically count as approved education.

I have a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

1. **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, are you paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep** (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He does live with me, but there's something I should mention - his other parent also lives with us and already claims Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that important detail.

This is a key point: **Only one person can get Child Benefit for the same child.** Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be eligible to claim it as well.

The rules state that two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child. If both parents are responsible for the child, you need to agree between yourselves who will claim it. If you cannot agree, HMRC will decide who gets it.

Since the other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you are **ineligible** to claim Child Benefit for him unless the other parent stops their claim and you make a new claim instead.

Just to confirm: **Is there any reason why you want to claim instead of the other parent, or are you looking to change who receives the Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. No, I was just curious about whether I could claim it myself, but if they're already getting it then that makes sense. So just to be clear - I'm not eligible because someone else is already claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's exactly right. You are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex because his other parent is already claiming it for him.

The rule is clear: only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child at any given time. Since Alex's other parent is already receiving Child Benefit for him, you cannot also claim it.

If you wanted to claim it instead in the future, the other parent would need to stop their claim first, and then you could make a new claim. But as things stand currently, with the other parent already claiming, you are ineligible.

Let me provide you with my formal assessment:
